 How it is for Kyiv these days 
 by 
 Alan Lipp 
 November 18, 2026 November 17, 2026 
 Share this:
 Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) 
 Facebook 
 Share on X (Opens in new window) 
 X 
 I recently spent 10 days in Kyiv, a European capital city that endures daily terrorism.
 Onix and Zircon anti-ship missiles that carry 1,000-pound warheads slammed into Kyiv and many other cities day and night. Russia launched almost 40 ballistic missiles, including North Korean KN-23s, in a one-night barrage.
 A nine-story apartment building was hit about 1 kilometer from me. Three people killed, 25 injured. I heard the impact. I felt the blast wave. A completely residential area.
 On Russia’s government-run version of CNN, the main host said Russia’s main problem with Ukrainians will be to figure out “where to bury them all.”
 Ukrainians know they are serious. Putin just called back Gen. Surovikin from Algeria to oversee a new approach to the destruction of Ukraine. Surovikin and the other top generals have committed to a plan of terrorism and destruction to force the evacuation of Kyiv.
 The Russians are targeting all power, heating, water and sewage infrastructure they can. They are targeting the business and food, equipment and warehouses. They are double-tapping the emergency personnel.
 They are targeting the bridges in Kyiv with jet-powered drones they flew into daytime traffic on one of Kyiv’s main arteries, the North Bridge.
 Russia is expected to be able to produce up to a third of a Hiroshima bomb’s worth of destructive power with the Geran 5 drones that fly at 3,000-4,000 feet and at over 300 mph.
 The Russians have already figured out how to keep enough Geran 5s in the air with modems to essentially have a dedicated satellite system for getting precise hits with their ballistic missiles.
 Europe could struggle to respond to that.
 On Russian CNN, the rabid imperialists that run the show called the West “idiots” for not realizing that after Ukraine, those 21-foot drones will be launched thousands at a time. That they are for “them.”
 Yes, the scale of Russia’s drone manufacturing plant, Alabuga, and Putin’s naked, bloodthirsty aggression should scare all freedom-loving people. They had a defense technology breakthrough that poses a great challenge right now for Western air defense.
 We cannot feed Ukraine to the Russian war machine.
 We cannot force Ukraine to give up its fortress belt that protects the plains in front of Kyiv and Kharkiv. We cannot let Ukraine be Russia’s outpost in future wars against Europe. America will have to step in to protect its largest trading partner, Europe.
 Sanction Russia. Give Kyiv old weapons. Sell new, effective weapons to Europe at a discount for themselves and Ukraine. Sanction China for buying Russian energy and giving Russia the jet engines for the drones.
 Alan Lipp lives in Park City and is active in Utah’s Ukrainian community. His writing has appeared in The Globalist and the Kyiv Independent.
